f: Definition 6.1 — Rational Asymptotes, Infinite Geometric Sums & Logarithm Laws
f_ar: تعريف 6.1 — الدوال الكسرية والمتتابعات والأسس واللوغاريتمات (SAAT)
b: For a rational function \( f(x) = \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)} \) of degrees \( m \) and \( n \): if \( m < n \), the horizontal asymptote is \( y = 0 \); if \( m = n \), it is \( y = \frac{\text{leading coeff of } P}{\text{leading coeff of } Q} \); common linear factors \( (x - c) \) create a point discontinuity (hole) at \( x = c \). An infinite geometric series converges if and only if \( |r| < 1 \), with sum \( S_\infty = \frac{a_1}{1 - r} \).
b_ar: For a rational function \( f(x) = \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)} \) of degrees \( m \) and \( n \): if \( m < n \), the horizontal asymptote is \( y = 0 \); if \( m = n \), it is \( y = \frac{\text{leading coeff of } P}{\text{leading coeff of } Q} \); common linear factors \( (x - c) \) create a point discontinuity (hole) at \( x = c \). An infinite geometric series converges if and only if \( |r| < 1 \), with sum \( S_\infty = \frac{a_1}{1 - r} \).
